I have been brewing 100% Kona coffee in my Keurig for many years.  I buy a variety of beans online and pay a premium for that privilege, but the result is worth it to me.  I have tried a variety of aftermarket k-ups, and ekobrew's version generally worked ok for me.  I bought their stainless steel version a year or two ago and those leaked and the hinge broke down, so I gave up on them and I am now on to this gold filter.  And it works well.  I have learned a few things over the years.  First, I actually think the coffee tastes better if after brewing it there is a small layer around the edge of bubbly slurm. I noticed this when drinking coffee freshly brewed in cafes in Europe, there was always some bubbly or foamy stuff around the edges.  Second, I find I get a better cup of coffee with a coarse to very coarse grind.  Third, don't overfill the Gold K-up, that actually interferes with the filtration.  If anything, underfill slightly.  Fourth, if you don't want the residue in the bottom of the cup, pour it into another cup.  I don't find my Keurig heats my coffee well enough so I brew it into a good mug and then heat it up some more.  That allows me to pour most of it into my travel mug and leave the residue behind.  Surely if you like coffee made in a French Press you are used to the coffee residue that ends up in the bottom of  your coffee and that is supposed to be a superior method of making coffee.

I found the grind of the bean is VERY sensitive. My first cup used grounds tailored to my K-cup genuine accessory. Very weak cup of coffee. I use a Mr. Coffee Burr grinder set between finest and drip. I had found any finer than this and the K-cup insert would leak from everywhere. Using the technique of "shimming up" the Keurig gasket, I could slow the leaking, not stop it. This MaxBrew does not leak. A good hinge with a pin and, an "O-ring" around the top.This is a huge thing. The Keurig relies on some pressure. I set the grinder to finest. No leaks and, a nice dark cup of Joe! It also means if you don't grind your own, you won't go wrong with an espresso grind.

One thing I observed with all Keurig's. If you watch the color of the brew as it exits the brewer, you will see it goes clear quickly. I think the true secret to the strongest cups of coffee in a Keurig is the amount you make. I use a clear cup. I load the grounds up and swap out the cup as soon as I think the color is to light. Measuring the cup of coffee, it is about 7 oz. Any more than that and there is significant dilution for my taste.
